setup.cli.openPort: If your hosting provider has its own firewall, open port {port}/tcp.

setup.cli.validUntil: Valid until {when} (24 h or until setup is complete).
setup.cli.validUntilBound: Valid until {when} (24 h or until setup is complete), only from the IP that opens it first.
setup.features.soon: Coming in this version of Kaskad: the feature is still being finished — this item will work after an update.
setup.jobs.busyCert: Still issuing the domain certificate — wait until it’s done.

setup.jobs.busyImport: Still moving the Kaskad 2.x settings — wait until it’s done.

setup.steps.amneziaDetail: {n} container in Docker · will keep working as now|{n} containers in Docker · will keep working as now
setup.steps.awgFileDetail: users, devices and AmneziaWG protocols from another Kaskad 3 server (gokaskad → 17)
setup.steps.awgFileNeeded: An AmneziaWG export file (JSON) is needed.
setup.steps.awgFileWait: moving users, devices and AmneziaWG protocols
setup.steps.backupApplied: Settings from the backup have been moved.
setup.steps.backupAgentsLater: agent keys {keys} — the setup does not bring them: an agent with such a key runs the server. You can bring them later, and only from your own copy: the panel’s “Settings” → “Upload backup” with the tick “Bring the AI agent keys of the copy” or menu 16 → 6 → 2
setup.steps.backupBlocked: This backup can’t be moved here yet: {blockers}
setup.steps.backupChanged: Something on the server changed after the preview — review the changes again.
setup.steps.backupConfirm: The move will replace what’s already on the server — confirm it.
setup.steps.backupDetail: a backup file with all settings
setup.steps.backupExpired: The backup is closed: more than 15 minutes have passed since it was opened (or the server was rebooted). Open the backup file again.
setup.steps.backupOpen: Backup opened: review what will be moved.
setup.steps.backupOpenConfirm: Backup opened: review what will change and confirm the move.
setup.steps.backupPreviewFirst: Open the backup first — we’ll show what will change, and only then move it.
setup.steps.backupReady: Settings backup is ready: save the file and write down the password.
setup.steps.certWait: Let’s Encrypt is checking the domain over port 80
setup.steps.collectorWait: The status collector hasn’t sent data yet — wait a few seconds.
setup.steps.dnsReady: The domain points to this server.
setup.steps.subNoSuch: No such subscription — reload the page.
setup.steps.exitsAlive: {alive} of {total} keys working — devices will go through the working ones
setup.steps.exitsChoiceBad: The choice is direct, exits or later.
setup.steps.exitsDirect: Devices will reach the internet from this server’s IP. You can add exits later in the panel.
setup.steps.exitsLaterDirect: For now devices go to the internet directly, from this server’s IP. Once you add exits in the panel, switch the route to them. The stage is marked as skipped: you can come back to it from the stage list.
setup.steps.exitsLaterKept: Exits are already there — the route wasn’t changed: devices reach the internet through them. The stage is marked as skipped: you can come back to it from the stage list.
setup.steps.finished: The wizard is closed. Its address no longer opens; to run it again — gokaskad → “Quick Start”.
setup.steps.fwd443: A TCP/443 forward takes the site’s port: the masking site and the panel on the domain won’t start on this server then. Pick another port here or confirm.
setup.steps.fwd443Short: port 443 is needed by the site
setup.steps.fwdBadAddr: The address is the IP of another server, for example 192.0.2.4.
setup.steps.fwdReachable: {host}:{port} is answering · {ms} ms — the forward will work.
setup.steps.fwdUdp: UDP can’t be checked in advance: we’ll check it when traffic flows.
setup.steps.fwdUnreachable: {host}:{port} isn’t answering over TCP — you can create the forward, but it won’t work until that server answers.
setup.steps.gatewayWait: turning on the gateway: DNS for devices, routing rules, modules
setup.steps.ghBad: The GitHub key didn’t work (revoked or expired): paste a new one.
setup.steps.ghNone: No GitHub key: without it the AmneziaWG core can’t be downloaded. Paste a ghp_… or github_pat_… key — it comes with Kaskad PRO.
setup.steps.ghSaved: The GitHub key works and is saved.
setup.steps.ghSavedUnchecked: Key saved without a check: GitHub didn’t answer.
setup.steps.ghUnchecked: GitHub key found, but GitHub isn’t answering right now — we’ll check it during installation.
setup.steps.goamneziaDetail: its own VPN on this server · left untouched; ports don’t overlap
setup.steps.hintLine31: The app may not support line 3.1 — we’ll issue AmneziaWG 2.0.
setup.steps.hintPort: The hosting provider may have closed the protocol’s port: open it in the hosting provider’s firewall (in the provider’s panel, the “Network” or “Firewall” section).
setup.steps.hintUdp: The mobile network may be cutting UDP — try Wi-Fi or issue settings for a TCP protocol.
setup.steps.importBotRow: stays as it was — same settings
setup.steps.importEgressRow: keys stay in the pool — you’ll see them at the “Exits” stage
setup.steps.importRolledBack: The move failed its check — everything is back as it was: {error}
setup.steps.moduleBuildingLong: building the kernel module — 1–3 minutes, the server keeps working
setup.steps.moduleCan: We’ll build the AmneziaWG kernel module — 1–3 minutes, the server keeps working. Half the CPU load.
setup.steps.moduleCannot: The kernel module isn’t possible here ({reasons}) — AmneziaWG will run in userspace (amneziawg-go).
setup.steps.noInbound: No protocols installed for this platform — go back to the “Mode and protocols” stage.
setup.steps.offline: The server has no internet: the step will wait. Check your payment and network with the hosting provider or reboot the server — the wizard checks the connection every 10 seconds.
setup.steps.passwordFirst: Set the panel password first — the “Welcome” stage.
setup.steps.passwordSet: Password set. From now on the wizard and the panel open only with it.
setup.steps.portBusyKind: {title} is not installed: port {port}/{protos} is used by another process — {why}.
setup.steps.portBusy: Port {port}/{protos} is in use: {why}. Free it and install again.
setup.steps.routeFailBad: “If exits are down” must be block or direct.
setup.steps.routeFailDirect: If the exits go down, traffic will go out from this server’s IP.
setup.steps.serverChecked: The wizard has checked the server.
setup.steps.siteDone: The domain now shows an ordinary site; the panel has moved to a new address.
setup.steps.siteEmailCleared: The email for Let’s Encrypt is removed.
setup.steps.siteVlessAnyway: Switch the site on and give the VLESS keys out again
setup.steps.domainVlessAnyway: Remove the domain and give the VLESS keys out again
setup.steps.siteWait: installing nginx, the site and the panel on the domain
setup.steps.subAlreadyAuto: This subscription is already added ({name}): its keys are in the pool, it refreshes once a day. No need to add it again.
setup.steps.subAlreadyManual: This subscription is already added ({name}): its keys are in the pool, it refreshes with the button in the panel. No need to add it again.
setup.steps.subFound: Subscription server found. “Add subscription” downloads it and adds its keys to the pool; it will refresh once a day.
setup.steps.subUnchecked: Couldn’t check the subscription link in advance (the name server didn’t answer quickly) — it will be checked when added.
setup.steps.undoDone: Undone: forwards are back in iptables.
setup.steps.undoNothing: The wizard hasn’t moved anything — nothing to undo.
setup.steps.vlessModeBad: The VLESS mode is tls or reality.
setup.steps.vlessModeTls: VLESS — TLS with your own domain, port 443.
setup.steps.vlessRisksBad: The version of the risks text looks like r1a.
setup.steps.vlessSiteBad: The masking site is a site name (for example, www.example.com).
setup.steps.vlessTls: TLS with your own domain, port 443
setup.web.certDomain: The connection is protected by a Let’s Encrypt certificate for the domain.
setup.web.certIp: The connection is protected by a Let’s Encrypt certificate for the IP · valid {lifetime}, renews automatically.
setup.web.certIpFailed: The IP certificate wasn’t issued. The browser will show a warning once — check the fingerprint.
setup.web.certIpFailedWhy: The IP certificate wasn’t issued: {why}. The browser will show a warning once — check the fingerprint.
setup.web.domainNotChecked: The domain {domain} hasn’t been checked at this step yet.
setup.web.linkExpired: The wizard link no longer works: {cmd}.
setup.web.linkExpiredAsk: The wizard link no longer works: get a new one in SSH — {cmd}.
setup.web.noPasswordYet: The password isn’t set yet: open the wizard with the link from SSH ({cmd}).
setup.web.notPublic: The panel isn’t open from the internet — there’s nowhere to move.
setup.web.openByLink: Open the wizard with the link from SSH ({cmd}).
setup.web.passwordString: The password must be a string.
setup.web.stageArgs: “kind” and “action” are required: open, done or skip.
setup.web.stubText: Quick Start wizard: the page isn’t built yet. API — /api/setup/*.
setup.web.tooManyTabs: The wizard is open in too many tabs — this one updates by polling.
setup.product.whyHy2: Phones and computers over UDP (v2RayTun, Hiddify, Karing); blocking of UDP in Russian mobile networks has not been checked
